claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand your situation with your children.

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?**

For Child Benefit eligibility, the rules vary based on age:
- **Under 16**: Usually automatically qualifying
- **16-19**: Must be in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Please tell me the age(s) of your child/children, and I'll guide you through the specific eligibility checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 8 years old (under 16), let me proceed with the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me ask: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

(For an 8-year-old, the answer would typically be "yes" since they wouldn't be in full-time work, but I need to confirm this with you.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh no, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8! He's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's great! Of course - Alex is in primary school at 8 years old, so that's definitely a "yes" to that question. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

For example, this would be benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that Alex personally receives (rather than as part of a family claim). For an 8-year-old, this would typically be "yes", but I need to confirm - is Alex receiving any of these benefits in their own name?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 8-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's a "yes" then - Alex is not receiving those benefits. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

For an 8-year-old in primary school, the answer would almost certainly be "no", but I need to confirm - is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8 and in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. So Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check your residency situation. There are several paths that can qualify:

**Where do you normally live?**

- Do you normally live in the UK? 
- Or do you have a particular immigration status (such as settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or are you a Crown servant living abroad)?

This is important for determining if you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Leeds.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward - you normally live in the UK, which meets the residency requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility means at least one of the following:
- You live with Alex
- You contribute to Alex's upkeep (such as paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.) - at least the equivalent amount of Child Benefit
- You're paying maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied for it?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. If there's another claimant:
- Are you both in agreement about who should claim?
- Or is there a dispute about who should be the claimant?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! So you're the only person claiming. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question: **Where is Alex currently living?**

- Does Alex live with you normally at home?
- Or is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or fostered?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, Alex has been in care with the local authority for a few months now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I need to understand the details of this care arrangement to check the eligibility rules.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **How long has Alex been in care?** (You mentioned "a few months" - is it less than 3 months, or longer than 3 months?)

2. **What type of care is it?** For example:
   - Is Alex in a children's home or residential care provided by the local authority?
   - Or is this a different type of care arrangement?

This information will help me determine if there are any impact on your Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been about 3 months now - so around 12 weeks or so. Alex is in a children's home run by the local authority.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me check the specific eligibility rules for this situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. This is an important check because there are special rules for children in care.

**The key question is: How much time does Alex spend at home with you?**

Specifically:
- Does Alex spend at least 24 hours per week at home with you? (For example, regular weekends or visiting time)
- Or does Alex stay at the children's home full-time with no regular time at home?

This matters because Child Benefit can continue for up to 8 weeks while a child is in care, but if they're in care for longer than 8 weeks AND don't spend at least 24 hours per week at home, the benefit stops. However, you may be able to claim again if Alex spends at least 2 consecutive nights per week at home, or 7 or more days in a row at home.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is at the children's home full-time. He doesn't come home regularly - I visit him there, but he doesn't spend time at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand. So Alex is in full-time care at the children's home and doesn't spend regular time at home with you. Since Alex has been in care for approximately 3 months (12 weeks), which is longer than the 8-week limit, and doesn't spend at least 24 hours per week at home, this means:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the eligibility rules, **you are currently ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Child Benefit can continue for the first 8 weeks while a child is in local authority care. However, after 8 weeks, eligibility stops unless the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you. Since Alex has been in care for approximately 12 weeks (longer than 8 weeks) and doesn't spend regular time at home, you no longer meet the eligibility criteria.

**However, there is a potential path forward:**

You **may be able to claim Child Benefit again** if:
- Alex spends at least **2 consecutive nights each week** at home with you, OR
- Alex spends **7 or more consecutive days at a time** at home with you

**What you should do:**

I'd recommend contacting HMRC directly to discuss your specific situation. They can:
- Confirm the exact dates and circumstances
- Advise you on whether any of the exceptions might apply
- Help you understand if the care arrangement might change in a way that could restore your eligibility

**Contact details:**
- Child Benefit helpline: 0300 200 3100
- Or visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand. Thank you for explaining that to me. It's disappointing, but I appreciate you walking me through the rules and letting me know what might change things in the future if Alex is able to spend more time at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome. I'm glad I could help you understand the situation clearly, even though it's disappointing news.

Let me formally record the outcome of your assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Your assessment has been recorded. I hope that Alex's situation improves and that you're able to spend more time together. If circumstances change - particularly if Alex is able to spend more time at home - please don't hesitate to get in touch with HMRC or come back for another assessment.

Wishing you and Alex all the best.

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and meets the initial qualifying criteria (under 16, not working full-time, not receiving benefits in own right, not in a disqualifying apprenticeship). The claimant lives in the UK (Leeds) and is responsible for Alex as their parent. However, Alex has been in full-time local authority care at a children's home for approximately 12 weeks (3 months). Child Benefit can only continue for up to 8 weeks when a child is in care, unless the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home. Since Alex has exceeded the 8-week threshold and does not spend regular time at home, the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex under the care duration rules.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant would normally qualify for Child Benefit for Alex, as all core eligibility criteria are met (child age, residency, responsibility, and no other claimants). However, the special rules for children in care apply here. Because Alex has been in local authority care for longer than 8 weeks and does not spend at least 24 hours per week at home, Child Benefit eligibility has ceased. The claimant may become eligible again if Alex's care arrangement changes and he spends at least 2 consecutive nights per week or 7+ consecutive days at home."
